findings.title: Conditional sequence flows are create-only through MCP
findings.why_it_matters: An MCP agent can create a conditional flow, but cannot change or clear its expression/language, rename it, retarget it, or delete just that flow. update_element and delete_element accept an elementId and route to element-only engine methods, while no connection update/delete tools exist. The only MCP workaround for a bad condition is deleting one of its endpoint elements, which also destroys unrelated flows and is not a safe parity action.
evidence: The public tool list provides connect plus update_element/delete_element, but no update_connection or delete_connection operation (src/server/tools.ts:232-272 and :369-411).

BpmnRequestHandler.updateElement and deleteElement call engine.updateElement/deleteElement with an elementId (src/server/handlers.ts:535-560); those engine methods look only in document elements/lanes and reject a sequence-flow ID as not found (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:366-383 and :428-445).
BpmnDocumentConnection stores label and condition metadata (src/types/index.ts:109-123), but SimpleBpmnEngine exposes no corresponding public mutation method.
findings.suggested_fix: Add connection lifecycle tools and engine operations that can update/clear label and condition metadata and delete a connection atomically. Reuse the current conditional/default validation, clear a source's default reference when its flow is deleted, and return the resulting structured connection for verification.

findings.title: Default-flow reassignment exists only as an undocumented properties escape hatch
findings.why_it_matters: The engine can reassign or clear a source's default flow through properties.defaultFlow, but neither the MCP schema nor README tells an agent that this key exists, that it must contain an outgoing sequence-flow ID, or that null clears it. Agents therefore see an isDefault creation flag but no discoverable inverse or reassignment action, despite the implementation accepting one through an untyped object.
evidence: update_element describes properties only as an arbitrary object with 'Properties to update' (src/server/tools.ts:369-387), and the README example shows only an assignee property (README.md:244-252).

SimpleBpmnEngine.updateElement specially interprets properties.defaultFlow/default and accepts null to clear it (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:390-421), behavior not represented in the public schema or docs.
The MCP schema documents isDefault only on connect (src/server/tools.ts:264-268), so tool discovery exposes creation but not reassignment/clear semantics.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose an explicit set_default_flow action (flow ID or null), or add a typed defaultFlow field to update_element with the ID/null semantics and source restrictions documented. Add a handler-level reassign/clear/reopen test.

findings.title: Connection creation and discovery do not provide a stable flow handle
findings.why_it_matters: connect discards the engine's returned connection and acknowledges only the endpoint IDs. list_elements exposes counts rather than flows, get_element cannot accept a flow ID, and condition details are available only by querying the source element's outgoing list. An agent can eventually inspect a known source, but cannot directly bind a successful call to the exact generated flow or retrieve an already known flow ID; this becomes ambiguous with repeated endpoints or overlapping callers and blocks safe follow-up manipulation.
evidence: SimpleBpmnEngine.connect returns BpmnDocumentConnection, including generated id, type, owner/scope, label, and condition (src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:268-279), but BpmnRequestHandler.connect ignores that return and emits prose only (src/server/handlers.ts:371-383).
list_elements returns only incoming/outgoing counts and a source defaultFlow ID (src/server/handlers.ts:453-469).
get_element resolves only elements/lanes and exposes condition metadata only inside a source element's outgoing array (src/server/handlers.ts:482-523).
findings.suggested_fix: Return structured connection metadata from connect and add get_connection/list_connections primitives (or make get_element explicitly accept connection IDs). Include id, type, source, target, ownerId, scopeId, label, condition, and isDefault.

residual_risks: connect descriptions do not enumerate the engine's eligible conditional/default sources: tasks, subprocesses/call activities, and exclusive/inclusive/complex gateways are accepted, while parallel/event-based gateways and events are rejected only at runtime.
get_element omits condition metadata on incoming records, so inspecting a target does not reveal why the path enters it; an agent must identify and query every source instead.
testing_gaps: No handler/e2e test exercises default-flow reassignment or clearing through the MCP request surface; the focused coverage calls SimpleBpmnEngine.updateElement directly.
No test covers editing or deleting a conditional flow because those MCP capabilities do not exist.
No test requires connect to return the generated flow ID and condition/default metadata.

The focused command `npx jest tests/integration/handlers.test.ts tests/unit/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.test.ts --runInBand` currently fails TypeScript compilation at tests/unit/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.test.ts:894 because BpmnDocumentElement is a union and defaultFlow is read without narrowing to kind === 'flowNode'; the handler suite passes.
